The teardown reveals internals identical to the two-year-old HTC U24 Pro, reinforcing earlier findings from an iFixit investigation. Swapping the motherboards between the two phones leaves both fully functional, further proving their shared hardware origins. Buying a phone is one thing. Watching someone scratch, bend, and rip it apart is an entirely different kind of satisfaction. The Trump Mobile T1 Phone has finally received that treatment from JerryRigEverything, and while it holds up surprisingly well against physical abuse, its insides tell a far less flattering story. YouTuber Zack Nelson put the gold-colored handset through his usual durability tests, starting with the display, which scratches at level six on the Mohs hardness scale, with deeper grooves appearing at level seven. That’s fairly standard for a modern smartphone. The metal frame also checks out, and despite attempts to bend the device from both directions, the T1 Phone survives without snapping or suffering an obvious structural failure.

title: The next big threat to RCS isn’t another messaging app
summary: The clock is ticking for RCS as AI threatens to rewrite the rules of messaging.
body: TL;DR GSMA Intelligence warns that the next six to twelve months could determine whether RCS leads the shift toward AI-powered conversations or follows rival platforms. Despite billions of daily RCS messages, commercial adoption remains relatively small, with the technology still largely focused on notifications. The GSMA is developing new conversational capabilities, but hasn’t announced specific features or release timelines. Six to twelve months. That’s how long GSMA Intelligence believes RCS has to establish itself as a serious player in the next era of messaging , or risk watching AI-powered conversations and rival platforms define that future without it. It’s an unusually urgent warning from the organization responsible for the messaging standard, especially as RCS adoption accelerates. But the concern isn’t whether people will continue sending messages. It’s whether those messages can do more than simply deliver information in a world where AI assistants are increasingly capable of acting on it .

Google is also introducing multi-turn ads in the US, allowing sponsored results to appear during follow-up questions in AI Mode. Google’s AI Mode is meant to make web searches easier. You ask a question, it pulls information from different websites, and you get a detailed answer without opening a dozen tabs. But as more people turn to AI Mode for everyday searches, Google is also finding new ways to show them ads. And if you’ve been enjoying an ad-free experience in AI Mode outside the US, that’s about to change. Google has announced that ads in AI Mode are expanding to 10 more countries, including India, Australia, Canada, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines, and Singapore.
